# verda registry (beta)

> Verda CLI **v1.10.0** · [other versions](https://github.com/verda-cloud/verda-cli/tags)

Manage the Verda Cloud Container Registry (vccr.io)

Manage Verda Container Registry (vccr.io) credentials, browse
repositories, push local Docker images, and copy images between
registries.

Credentials are stored separately from API credentials in
~/.verda/credentials using verda_registry_ prefixed keys.

Aliases: `vccr`, `vcr`

Subcommands:

- [`verda registry configure`](#verda-registry-configure): Configure Verda Container Registry credentials
- [`verda registry configure-docker`](#verda-registry-configure-docker): Set up Docker/compose/helm to pull from VCR (writes ~/.docker/config.json)
- [`verda registry copy`](#verda-registry-copy): Copy an image between registries
- [`verda registry delete`](#verda-registry-delete): Delete a repository or a single image
- [`verda registry ls`](#verda-registry-ls): List repositories in the active Verda project
- [`verda registry push`](#verda-registry-push): Push local images to the container registry
- [`verda registry show`](#verda-registry-show): Show Verda Container Registry credential status
- [`verda registry tags`](#verda-registry-tags): List tags in a container repository

## verda registry configure

Configure Verda Container Registry credentials

Save Verda Container Registry credentials to ~/.verda/credentials
(override with --credentials-file or VERDA_REGISTRY_CREDENTIALS_FILE).
Stored with verda_registry_ prefixed keys alongside API and S3 keys;
other keys in the profile are preserved.

Three ways to provide credentials:

```text
• interactive — run with no flags on a terminal; the wizard guides you,
  including where to find the credential in the web UI.
• --paste — paste the web UI's "Registry authentication command" (the
  docker login … line); the host is auto-detected.
• --username + --password-stdin [--endpoint] — Docker-style; --endpoint
  defaults to the profile's saved host, else vccr.io.
```

Find the credential in the web UI under: select project → Credentials →
Create credentials.

**Usage**

```text
verda registry configure [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --credentials-file string                         Path to the shared credentials file
      --docker-config verda registry configure-docker   Also write ~/.docker/config.json (same merge as verda registry configure-docker)
      --endpoint string                                 Registry host (e.g. "vccr.io"). Defaults to the saved endpoint for this profile, or "vccr.io" on production.
      --expires-in int                                  Days from now until the credentials expire (default 30)
      --password-stdin                                  Read the registry secret from stdin
      --paste docker login ...                          Full docker login ... command to parse (alternative to --username/--password-stdin)
      --profile string                                  Credentials profile name (default: active profile)
      --username string                                 Registry username (vcr-<project-id>+<name>)
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Interactive wizard (recommended for first-time setup)
verda registry configure

# Paste the web UI's "Registry authentication command"
verda registry configure --paste "docker login -u vcr-abc+cli -p s3cret vccr.io"

# Username + secret on stdin (--endpoint defaults to vccr.io)
echo -n "$SECRET" | verda registry configure --username vcr-abc+cli --password-stdin
```

## verda registry configure-docker

Set up Docker/compose/helm to pull from VCR (writes ~/.docker/config.json)

Write the active Verda Container Registry credentials into the Docker
config file so third-party tools (docker pull, docker-compose,
helm pull oci://, nerdctl) can authenticate against the registry.

This command does NOT talk to the registry; it is a local file merge.
Existing entries for other registries, as well as unknown top-level
keys (credsStore, credHelpers, HttpHeaders, ...), are preserved
verbatim.

Default Docker config path: ~/.docker/config.json
Override with --config or DOCKER_CONFIG.

**Usage**

```text
verda registry configure-docker [flags]
```

Aliases: `login`

**Flags**

```text
      --config string             Path to the Docker config file (default ~/.docker/config.json)
      --credentials-file string   Path to the shared Verda credentials file
      --profile string            Credentials profile to read (default: active profile)
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Write the default profile into ~/.docker/config.json
verda registry configure-docker

# Use a specific profile
verda registry configure-docker --profile staging

# Write to a non-default Docker config file
verda registry configure-docker --config /tmp/docker/config.json
```

## verda registry copy

Copy an image between registries

Copy a single image from a source registry to the configured
Verda Container Registry.

The source must be a fully qualified reference (e.g.
"docker.io/library/nginx:1.25"). The destination, if omitted,
defaults to the active registry endpoint + project with the
source repository and tag preserved. A short destination
(e.g. "my-app:prod") is expanded via the active credentials
to "&lt;endpoint&gt;/&lt;project&gt;/my-app:prod".

Source-side credentials are resolved via ~/.docker/config.json
and registered credential helpers by default. Pass
--src-auth anonymous to skip the keychain entirely or
--src-auth basic plus --src-username / --src-password-stdin
to supply explicit credentials. Run with no arguments on a terminal to launch an interactive wizard that prompts for the source, access mode, scope (this tag / all tags), and destination, then runs the copy.

**Usage**

```text
verda registry copy <src> [<dst>] [flags]
```

Aliases: `cp`

**Flags**

```text
      --all-tags                  Copy every tag in the source repository
      --credentials-file string   Path to credentials file
      --dry-run                   Resolve and summarize what would be copied; no writes. Ignores --overwrite.
      --image-jobs int            Image-level parallelism for --all-tags (0 = auto)
      --jobs int                  Layer-level parallelism (0 = ggcr default)
      --overwrite                 Allow replacing an existing destination tag (ignored under --dry-run)
      --profile string            Credentials profile name (default: active profile)
      --progress string           Progress output: auto|plain|json|none (default "auto")
      --retries int               Maximum attempts for idempotent HTTP operations on transient errors (default 5)
      --src-auth string           Source authentication mode: docker-config|anonymous|basic (default "docker-config")
      --src-password-stdin        Read the source registry password from stdin (required with --src-auth basic)
      --src-username string       Source registry username (required with --src-auth basic)
      --yes                       Skip the overwrite confirmation prompt; implies --overwrite
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Copy a public image from Docker Hub to VCR under the same repo/tag
verda registry copy docker.io/library/nginx:1.25

# Copy to a custom destination
verda registry copy gcr.io/my-project/app:v1 my-app:prod

# Use basic auth on the source side
echo "$SRC_PASSWORD" | verda registry copy \
private.example.com/app:v1 \
--src-auth basic --src-username jdoe --src-password-stdin

# JSON output for scripts
verda registry copy docker.io/library/nginx:1.25 -o json
```

## verda registry delete

Delete a repository or a single image

Delete a repository or a single image (artifact) from the active
Verda project.

A bare repository argument removes the repository and every
artifact / tag under it (equivalent to Harbor's "Delete image
repository" button). Appending :TAG or @DIGEST scopes the
delete to a single artifact — the same semantics as the web
UI's per-row "Delete image": the manifest and every tag that
pointed at it are removed in one call.

Without an argument on a terminal, delete enters an interactive
flow: pick a repository, then choose between deleting selected
images or the whole repository. Piping or redirecting stdout
disables the interactive flow — scripts must always pass an
explicit target. Agent mode (--agent) requires --yes for every
destructive operation, matching the safety contract used by
`verda vm delete`.

**Usage**

```text
verda registry delete [REPOSITORY[:TAG|@DIGEST]] [flags]
```

Aliases: `del`, `rm`

**Flags**

```text
      --credentials-file string   Path to the shared Verda credentials file
      --profile string            Credentials profile to read (default: active profile)
  -y, --yes                       Skip confirmation (required in agent mode)
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Interactive: pick a repo, then delete images or the whole repo
verda registry delete

# Delete a whole repository (all artifacts, all tags)
verda registry delete library/hello-world

# Delete a single artifact by tag
verda registry delete library/hello-world:latest

# Delete a single artifact by digest
verda registry delete library/hello-world@sha256:d1a8d0a4eeb6

# Skip confirmation (required in agent mode)
verda registry delete library/hello-world --yes
```

## verda registry ls

List repositories in the active Verda project

List every repository in the Verda project associated with the
active registry credentials. Repositories are resolved via
Harbor's REST API, not the Docker Registry v2 catalog endpoint —
the catalog endpoint is admin-only on Harbor and is not
accessible to the project-scoped robot accounts VCR issues.

When run on a terminal, selecting a repository drills into its
per-artifact details (digest, tags, size, push/pull times).
When piped to a file or another command (or when -o json/yaml
is set), ls prints a single non-interactive document.

**Usage**

```text
verda registry ls [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --credentials-file string   Path to the shared Verda credentials file
      --profile string            Credentials profile to read (default: active profile)
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Interactive: pick a repo to see its image list
verda registry ls

# Non-interactive table (piping suppresses the picker)
verda registry ls | less

# JSON output for scripts
verda registry ls -o json

# Use a non-default credentials profile
verda registry ls --profile staging
```

## verda registry push

Push local images to the container registry

Upload one or more local images to Verda Container Registry.

Each positional argument is a local reference resolved through
the --source pipeline:

```text
- auto   (default) picks oci for directories, tar for .tar/.tar.gz
         files, and daemon for everything else after probing the
         Docker daemon.
- daemon reads the image from the local Docker daemon.
- oci    reads an OCI image layout from a directory.
- tar    reads a Docker/OCI tarball from a file.
```

The destination repository defaults to the local reference's
repository name under the active credentials' project; use
--repo / --tag to override (single-image only).

For v1 images are pushed sequentially; parallelism across
images will arrive with the interactive progress view.

**Usage**

```text
verda registry push <local-image> [<local-image>...] [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --credentials-file string   Path to credentials file
      --image-jobs int            Image-level parallelism (v1: always 1) (default 1)
      --jobs int                  Layer-level parallelism (0 = ggcr default)
      --no-mount                  Disable cross-repo blob mount (v1: flag is a no-op)
      --profile string            Credentials profile name (default: active profile)
      --progress string           Progress output: auto|plain|json|none (default "auto")
      --repo string               Override destination repository name (single-image only)
      --retries int               Maximum attempts for idempotent HTTP operations on transient errors (default 5)
      --source string             Image source: auto|daemon|oci|tar (default "auto")
      --tag string                Override destination tag (single-image only)
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Push a single image from the Docker daemon
verda registry push my-app:v1

# Push multiple images sequentially
verda registry push my-app:v1 worker:v1 edge:v1

# Push with a different destination repo and tag
verda registry push my-app:latest --repo team/api --tag prod

# Push from an OCI layout directory
verda registry push --source oci ./build/image

# Push from a tarball
verda registry push --source tar ./out/image.tar

# JSON output for scripts
verda registry push my-app:v1 -o json
```

## verda registry show

Show Verda Container Registry credential status

Show the current Verda Container Registry credential status for a
profile. The secret is never displayed — only whether credentials
are loaded, their username, endpoint, project id, and expiry.

If no credentials are configured for the profile, the command
reports "not configured" and exits 0.

**Usage**

```text
verda registry show [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --credentials-file string   Path to the shared credentials file
      --profile string            Credentials profile to show (default: active profile)
```

**Examples**

```bash
# Show the default profile
verda registry show

# Show a specific profile
verda registry show --profile staging

# JSON output (e.g. for scripting)
verda registry show -o json
```

## verda registry tags

List tags in a container repository

List every tag in the given repository plus per-tag metadata
(digest, size). On a terminal, tags are shown as an interactive,
filterable picker — select one to print its full pull reference and
exit (the same picker "verda registry ls" uses when you drill into a
repository). Piped output, -o json/yaml, or --agent print the table
instead.

The repository may be passed as a full reference
("vccr.io/&lt;project&gt;/&lt;name&gt;") or a short reference ("&lt;name&gt;"). Short
references are expanded using the active registry credentials. If
a tag component is included in the argument (e.g. "app:v1"), it is
ignored — tags always operates on the full repository.

The full tag list is always fetched from the registry. Per-tag
HEAD lookups for digest/size are capped by --limit to keep
response time bounded on repositories with many tags. Tags past
the cap are listed by name with "--" in the DIGEST and SIZE
columns.

Pass --all to run HEAD lookups for every tag regardless of
--limit. --limit 0 is equivalent to --all.

The "PUSHED" column is reserved for a future release and currently
prints "--" for every row.

**Usage**

```text
verda registry tags <repo> [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --all                       Run metadata lookups for every tag (overrides --limit)
      --credentials-file string   Path to the shared Verda credentials file
      --limit int                 Cap on per-tag metadata lookups (0 = unlimited) (default 50)
      --profile string            Credentials profile to read (default: active profile)
```

**Examples**

```bash
# List tags in a short-form repository
verda registry tags my-app

# List tags in a fully qualified repository
verda registry tags vccr.io/my-project/my-app

# Raise the metadata cap
verda registry tags my-app --limit 200

# Metadata for every tag (slower on repositories with many tags)
verda registry tags my-app --all

# JSON output for scripts
verda registry tags my-app -o json
```

---

Global flags such as `--output`, `--agent` and `--debug` work with every command: see [Global Flags](../commands.md#global-flags).
